The diffs fix netrc parsing, not the redirect check, so the lesson would not transfer; left out to keep the family crisp.

Commit 3f9d49f9e3df56a168312a2863fc9461da3d6b8f (2026-06-04, 'use raw Punycode when deciding if we should copy headers on redirect') is a real recurrence of the Go redirect bug, but no advisory references it (GO-2026-5026 is about x/net/idna).
Commits fbe07f1a79d4bd8142ada44b562c8dd14e005149 and 131a72736f59fb00185b1974806f5ad8ede46717 (July 2026) fix further redirect header issues, but no advisory was found for them.
Cookies forwarded to third parties on redirect; the linked fix 65ab7d5caaaf2f95e61f9dd65441801c2ddee38b is a 30-file feature commit (new session cookie format) where the fix is buried.
Linked fix commit c071f95336a987dad9332fd388adeb249925cc57 returns 404 on GitHub.
Not checked in depth: CVE-2022-29248 is cookie-jar domain matching, CVE-2026-67339 sends Proxy-Authorization to origins outside a redirect context.

Further 2026 advisories of the same family found in the GitHub database (reactor-netty, async-http-client, urllib (npm), kiota, dio, rclone, datamodel-code-generator, linuxfabrik-lib, apprise, openclaw, gix-transport) but not fetched or verified for lack of time. They would only add to the evaluation side.
No fix: the advisory marks no patched version and its only commit link (fea250ac6eacd56f90a82fbe2481cfdbb9a1bbd1) edits the README.
No patched version (destination symlinks followed); linked PR #575 not merged into a release.
Upstream is unmaintained and has no patched version; the maintained fork's fix is listed as CVE-2026-53486.
FastZip base-directory prefix flaw introduced by the 2018 fix; no commit in v1.3.2...v1.3.3 touches FastZip or WindowsNameTransform, so no verifiable fix commit.
Advisory has no fix link and no fix commit was located.
Several archive/symlink advisories (2022, 2025) not examined for lack of time.
Text-format map parsing mutates the returned map's prototype (2026); not fetched or verified.

advisories.summary: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor in Requests

instances.mechanism: When a redirect pointed to a different host, the session kept the Authorization header built from ~/.netrc for the first host; the fix deletes it on hostname change and recomputes netrc credentials for the new host.
instances.notes: Advisory links only issue #1885; fix is PR #1892 (merged into the 2.3.0 line). GitHub's merge_commit_sha for that PR (e13e1152abf023d7903e9eb0ebab0fd35c626d9b) is a test-merge that is not on main, so the two PR commits are recorded instead. No test file in these commits.

advisories.summary: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor in Requests

instances.mechanism: The Proxy-Authorization header of the original request was replayed unchanged on every redirect; the fix recomputes proxy settings and the proxy credential header for each redirect target, dropping them when the new URL bypasses the proxy.
instances.notes: Advisory links only issue #1885; HISTORY.md for 2.3.0 names CVE-2014-1830. The rebuild_proxies() method introduced here is the code path that later caused CVE-2023-32681 (same repository).

advisories.summary: rest-client Gem Vulnerable to Session Fixation

fix_commits.message_title: Add cookie jar for handling HTTP redirection.
fix_commits.role: PR commit: cookie jar for redirects

fix_commits.message_title: Fix up cookie redirect functionality and tests.

instances.mechanism: Cookies received in a redirect response were copied into the follow-up request whatever its host; the fix stores them in a domain-aware cookie jar so they are only sent where the cookie domain matches.
instances.notes: Advisory frames it as session fixation (Set-Cookie values of the redirect response forwarded to an arbitrary redirect target). Fix found through issue #369 timeline; the advisory has no commit link.

advisories.summary: libcurl 7.1 through 7.57.0 might accidentally leak authentication data to third parties. When...

fix_commits.message_title: http: prevent custom Authorization headers in redirects

instances.mechanism: Authorization headers supplied as custom headers were re-sent on every redirect, including to other hosts; the fix skips them on follows to a different host unless CURLOPT_UNRESTRICTED_AUTH allows it.
instances.notes: Fix commit taken from curl's advisory (curl-www docs/CVE-2018-1000007.md, short SHA af32cd3859336ab resolved through the GitHub API).

advisories.summary: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor in urllib3

fix_commits.message_title: Remove Authorization header when redirecting cross-host (#1346)

instances.mechanism: PoolManager followed cross-host redirects with the caller's Authorization header; the fix adds Retry.remove_headers_on_redirect (Authorization by default) and strips those headers when the redirect leaves the host.
instances.notes: The header comparison added here was case-sensitive, which is CVE-2018-25091.

advisories.summary: Insufficiently Protected Credentials in Requests

fix_commits.message_title: Strip Authorization header whenever root URL changes
Rework authorization stripping logic as discussed

instances.mechanism: Authorization was only removed when the hostname changed, so an https to http redirect on the same host sent credentials in clear text; the fix also strips it when scheme or port change, keeping only the http-to-https upgrade on default ports.
instances.notes: Same function (rebuild_auth) as the 2014 fix: the hostname-only comparison from 2014 was the incomplete part.

advisories.summary: Authorization Header forwarded on redirect

fix_commits.message_title: Remove Authorization headers regardless of case on cross-origin redirects (#1511)

instances.mechanism: The redirect strip list from the CVE-2018-20060 fix compared header names case-sensitively, so a lower-case 'authorization' header still crossed origins; the fix lowercases both the configured names and the request headers before removing them.
instances.notes: Incomplete fix that came back in the same repository: the advisory says this exists because the CVE-2018-20060 fix was case-sensitive. Fixed in Dec 2018 but the advisory was only published in Oct 2023 (straddles the cutoff).

advisories.summary: Http request which redirect to another hostname do not strip authorization header in @actions/http-client

instances.mechanism: The client reissued redirected requests with all original headers, including Authorization, even when the redirect went to another hostname; the fix deletes the authorization header (any case) when the hostname changes.
instances.notes: Repository is archived (code now lives in actions/toolkit).

advisories.summary: Exposure of sensitive information in follow-redirects

instances.mechanism: Only the Authorization header was dropped on a cross-domain redirect, so a Cookie header set by the caller was forwarded to the third-party host; the fix adds Cookie to the removed headers.

advisories.summary: node-fetch forwards secure headers to untrusted sites

fix_commits.message_title: fix(Headers): don't forward secure headers to 3th party (#1449)
fix_commits.role: primary (v3, squash of PR #1449 on main)

fix_commits.message_title: fix(Headers): don't forward secure headers to 3th party
fix_commits.role: PR head commit linked by the advisory (not on main)

instances.mechanism: fetch() copied Authorization, Cookie and related headers into the follow-up request for any redirect target; the fix deletes them unless the new host equals or is a subdomain of the original one.
instances.notes: The advisory also links 36e47e8a6406185921e4985dcbeff140d73eaa10, which is only the 3.1.1 release commit (changelog and version bump), so it is not recorded as a fix commit.

advisories.summary: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor in follow-redirects

instances.mechanism: Confidential headers were kept whenever the host stayed the same, even if the redirect downgraded the scheme; the fix also drops them when the protocol changes.
instances.notes: Second fix in the same function within a month (after CVE-2022-0155).

advisories.summary: Forwarding of confidentials headers to third parties in fluture-node

fix_commits.message_title: Update redirection strategies to drop confidential headers
Fix notion of cross-origin to include scheme changes

instances.mechanism: The redirection strategies reissued the original request with every header to the Location host; the fix drops authorization and cookie headers when the target is not the same host or a subdomain, and a same-day follow-up also treats a downgrade of the scheme as cross-origin.
instances.notes: The advisory references psf/requests PR #4718 as prior art.

advisories.summary: Incorrect Authorization and Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor in scrapy

instances.mechanism: Redirect requests inherited the original request's cookies and Cookie header, so they were sent to whatever domain the redirect named; the fix rebuilds the redirect request without the cookies argument and drops a manual Cookie header when the netloc changes.

advisories.summary: A insufficiently protected credentials vulnerability in fixed in curl 7.83.0 might leak...

fix_commits.message_title: http: avoid auth/cookie on redirects same host diff port

instances.mechanism: The check that keeps auth and cookie headers for the original host compared only the host name, so a redirect to the same host on another port or protocol got them; the fix records the first port and protocol and requires all three to match.
instances.notes: Recurrence of CVE-2018-1000007 in the same function (host-only comparison).

advisories.summary: An insufficiently protected credentials vulnerability exists in curl 4.9 to and include curl 7.82...

fix_commits.message_title: transfer: redirects to other protocols or ports clear auth
openssl: don't leak the SRP credentials in redirects either
fix_commits.role: follow-up (TLS-SRP credentials), listed as Fixed-in by curl

instances.mechanism: Stored user name and password were kept when a redirect stayed on the same host but switched port or protocol; the fix clears them in Curl_follow when the port or scheme differs from the original connection.
instances.notes: Fix spans two commits; curl's advisory lists the second one as Fixed-in.

advisories.summary: Mechanize before v2.8.5 vulnerable to authorization header leak on port redirect

instances.mechanism: Credential headers were only removed when the redirect changed host, so a redirect to another port of the same host kept Authorization; the fix also strips Authorization on a port change while keeping cookies.

advisories.summary: Failure to strip the Cookie header on change in host or HTTP downgrade
Fix failure to strip Authorization header on HTTP downgrade

instances.mechanism: The redirect middleware removed only Authorization and only on a host change, so Cookie crossed hosts and Authorization survived an https to http downgrade; the fix strips both headers on host change or downgrade.
instances.notes: One commit fixes two advisories.

advisories.summary: CURLOPT_HTTPAUTH option not cleared on change of origin
Change in port should be considered a change in origin

instances.mechanism: The origin test ignored the port and the cURL-level credentials (CURLOPT_HTTPAUTH, CURLOPT_USERPWD) were never cleared on redirect; the fix uses a full cross-origin comparison for both the headers and the cURL options.
instances.notes: Second guzzle fix eleven days after the previous one, same file (RedirectMiddleware.php).

advisories.summary: undici before v5.8.0 vulnerable to uncleared cookies on cross-host / cross-origin redirect

instances.mechanism: The redirect handler removed Authorization but not Cookie when the new origin was unknown; the fix adds Cookie to the headers dropped on cross-origin redirects.

advisories.summary: scs-library-client may leak user credentials to third-party service via HTTP redirect

fix_commits.message_title: fix: omit credentials for redirected URLs
fix: remove extraneous Authorization HTTP header in range request #153

instances.mechanism: Image downloads followed the Location of a redirect and attached the library bearer token to it regardless of host; the fix only sends credentials when the redirect keeps the same scheme and host.
instances.notes: No test file changed in these commits.

advisories.summary: Unintended leak of Proxy-Authorization header in requests

instances.mechanism: On redirects rebuild_proxies re-added a Proxy-Authorization header to the request itself, which for an HTTPS (tunnelled) destination is delivered to the origin server; the fix only sets that header for non-HTTPS targets.
instances.notes: Introduced by the CVE-2014-1830 fix in the same repository (the advisory says requests leaked since 2.3.0).

advisories.summary: `Cookie` HTTP header isn't stripped on cross-origin redirects

instances.mechanism: The default list of headers removed on cross-origin redirects contained only Authorization, so an explicit Cookie header followed the redirect; the fix adds Cookie to the default list.

advisories.summary: Undici's cookie header not cleared on cross-origin redirect in fetch

instances.mechanism: The fetch() redirect path deleted only authorization on a cross-origin redirect, unlike the dispatcher fixed in 2022; the fix also deletes cookie and host there.
instances.notes: Same bug as CVE-2022-31151 in a second code path of the same repository.

advisories.summary: Undici proxy-authorization header not cleared on cross-origin redirect in fetch

instances.mechanism: fetch() still forwarded Proxy-Authorization on cross-origin redirects; the fix deletes it next to authorization and cookie.

advisories.summary: Scrapy authorization header leakage on cross-domain redirect

instances.mechanism: The redirect middleware removed a manual Cookie header on domain change but left Authorization in place; the fix removes Authorization under the same condition.
instances.notes: The advisory only links the 1.8 branch merge; the 2.11 merge was found in the 2.11 branch history.

advisories.summary: When following an HTTP redirect to a domain which is not a subdomain match or exact match of the...

fix_commits.message_title: net/http, net/http/cookiejar: avoid subdomain matches on IPv6 zones

instances.mechanism: The subdomain test used for forwarding sensitive headers and cookies was a plain suffix match, so an IPv6 literal with a zone such as ::1%.www.example.com counted as a subdomain; the fix refuses suffix matching for hosts containing ':' or '%'.
instances.notes: Commit found by searching golang/go for Gerrit CL 569340 (go.dev/cl/569340), the fix link of GO-2024-2600.

advisories.summary: follow-redirects' Proxy-Authorization header kept across hosts

instances.mechanism: The header filter applied on cross-host redirects matched authorization and cookie but not proxy-authorization; the fix extends the regular expression.

advisories.summary: Undici's Proxy-Authorization header not cleared on cross-origin redirect for dispatch, request, stream, pipeline

fix_commits.role: backport (5.x, also adds a header-name helper)

instances.mechanism: After fetch() was fixed, the redirect handler used by request, stream, pipeline and dispatch still kept Proxy-Authorization on cross-origin redirects; the fix adds it to the headers removed for unknown origins.
instances.notes: Fourth undici advisory of this family; each one patched one header in one of two code paths.

advisories.summary: Scrapy leaks the authorization header on same-domain but cross-origin redirects

instances.mechanism: Authorization was only dropped when the netloc changed, so a same-host redirect from https to http kept it; the fix compares scheme, host and default ports and drops Authorization on any of them changing.
instances.notes: Incomplete fix three months earlier (CVE-2024-3574) in the same function. On master the change arrived inside a combined commit (d2f1e00a6afa46c26a334a24217d5bf605bab9fb, 'Merge 2.11.2 changes'), so the 2.11 branch merge is recorded.

advisories.summary: urllib3's Proxy-Authorization request header isn't stripped during cross-origin redirects

instances.mechanism: A Proxy-Authorization header set manually (without urllib3's proxy support) was not in the default strip list and followed cross-origin redirects; the fix adds it to the list.

advisories.summary: fetch: Authorization headers not dropped when redirecting cross-origin

instances.mechanism: Deno's fetch() redirect step kept every request header, so Authorization, Proxy-Authorization and Cookie reached a different origin; the fix removes them when the redirect changes origin.
instances.notes: Advisory has no commit link; the fix is the 'Merge commit from fork' on ext/fetch dated 2024-11-25, just before deno 2.1.2. Deno's documentation previously said it did not need to protect against this because it had no origin concept.

advisories.summary: The HTTP client drops sensitive headers after following a cross-domain redirect. For example, a...

fix_commits.message_title: net/http: persist header stripping across repeated redirects

instances.mechanism: The decision to drop sensitive headers was made per hop against the previous request, so a.com to b.com/1 to b.com/2 put Authorization back on the last hop; the fix makes stripping sticky once a cross-domain hop has happened.
instances.notes: Commit found by searching golang/go for issue 70530 (fix link go.dev/cl/643100). The commit also regenerates a test certificate in net/http/internal/testcert.

advisories.summary:
When an OAuth2 bearer token is used for an HTTP(S) transfer, and that transfer
performs a cross...

fix_commits.message_title: curl_sasl: if redirected, require permission to use bearer

instances.mechanism: After a redirect from HTTP to a SASL protocol such as IMAP or SMTP, the OAuth2 bearer token was still offered to the new server; the fix only uses the bearer token on a followed request when auth to other hosts is explicitly allowed.

advisories.summary: AIOHTTP leaks Cookie and Proxy-Authorization headers on cross-origin redirect

fix_commits.role: backport (3.13), the commit linked by the advisory

instances.mechanism: On a cross-origin redirect the client dropped auth and Authorization but kept Cookie and Proxy-Authorization headers; the fix pops both as well.

advisories.summary:
When an OAuth2 bearer token is used for an HTTP(S) transfer, and that transfer
performs a...

fix_commits.message_title: http: only send bearer if auth is allowed

instances.mechanism: When the redirect target had an entry in .netrc, curl sent the first host's OAuth2 bearer token to it because the Bearer header path skipped the per-host permission check used for other credentials; the fix adds that check.
instances.notes: Same oversight as CVE-2025-14524 two months later, this time in lib/http.c.

advisories.summary: follow-redirects leaks Custom Authentication Headers to Cross-Domain Redirect Targets

instances.mechanism: Only three hard-coded header names were removed on cross-domain redirects, so custom credential headers such as X-API-Key reached the new host; the fix lets callers declare extra sensitive headers to strip.
instances.notes: No CVE. The fix is opt-in (new sensitiveHeaders option), so default behaviour for custom headers is unchanged.

advisories.summary:
curl might erroneously pass on credentials for a first proxy to a second
proxy.

This can happen...

fix_commits.message_title: http: clear the proxy credentials as well on port or scheme change

instances.mechanism: When a redirect changed scheme and therefore made curl use a different, credential-less proxy, the first proxy's credentials were still sent; the fix restores proxy credentials from the options on every follow (and user credentials when port or scheme change).

advisories.summary: go-git: Credential leak via cross-host redirect in smart HTTP transport

fix_commits.role: primary (merge of PR #1997 on main, v6)

fix_commits.message_title: plumbing: transport/http, Add support for followRedirects policy

instances.mechanism: The smart-HTTP transport moved its endpoint to wherever /info/refs redirected and kept sending the stored credentials there; the fix limits redirects to the initial request by default and clears user, password and auth when the redirect changes host or port.
instances.notes: Advisory links only release tags; the v5 backport was found in the releases/v5.x history right before v5.18.0 and points to PR #1997 on main.

advisories.summary: Axios: Proxy-Authorization header leaks to redirect target when proxy is re-evaluated to direct connection

fix_commits.message_title: fix: clear stale header on redirect when target is no-proxy (#10794)

instances.mechanism: A Proxy-Authorization header added for a proxied first request stayed in the headers when the redirect target was reached directly or through another proxy; the fix deletes any stale Proxy-Authorization (any case) when the proxy is re-evaluated on redirect.

advisories.summary: @hapi/wreck leaks sensitive `Proxy-Authorization` header across cross-hostname redirects

instances.mechanism: Cross-hostname redirects removed authorization and cookie but not proxy-authorization; the fix uses a set of sensitive headers that includes it.

advisories.summary: urllib3: Sensitive headers forwarded across origins in proxied low-level redirects

instances.mechanism: Header stripping on cross-origin redirects lived only in PoolManager, so redirects followed by a lower-level connection pool (for example one from ProxyManager.connection_from_url) kept Authorization, Cookie and Proxy-Authorization; the fix applies the same stripping in HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen.
instances.notes: Advisory has no commit link; the 'Merge commit from fork' before the 2.7.0 release adds changelog/GHSA-qccp-gfcp-xxvc.bugfix.rst. Fifth urllib3 advisory in this family.

advisories.summary: async-http-client: Cookie header not stripped on cross-origin redirect

instances.mechanism: When stripping credentials for a cross-origin or downgrade redirect, the interceptor removed Authorization and Proxy-Authorization but not an explicit Cookie header; the fix removes Cookie too and lets the cookie store re-add matching cookies.
instances.notes: The advisory links the short SHA 3b0e3e9e; the full SHA was resolved through the API.

advisories.summary: @hapi/wreck: Sensitive credential headers leak across cross-port and cross-scheme redirects

fix_commits.message_title: fix: cross-origin redirect should also remove sensitive headers

instances.mechanism: The sensitive-header check compared only hostnames, so a redirect to another port or scheme on the same host kept credentials; the fix compares full origins.
instances.notes: Second wreck fix in two weeks, same block of code.

advisories.summary: Tornado: Authorization header forwarded across cross-origin redirects in SimpleAsyncHTTPClient

fix_commits.message_title: simple_httpclient: Strip auth headers on cross-origin redirects

instances.mechanism: SimpleAsyncHTTPClient copied all headers and basic-auth settings onto the redirected request; the fix clears Authorization, Cookie, auth_username/auth_password and URL userinfo when scheme or netloc changes.
instances.notes: Advisory has no commit link; found by searching tornado commits. The code comment cites libcurl's behaviour as the model.

advisories.summary: Excon does not redact additional sensitive/risky headers when following redirects

instances.mechanism: The redirect follower removed Authorization and proxy headers but forwarded Cookie, Cookie2 and common token headers; the fix redacts a longer list on every redirect and removes the middleware that copied Set-Cookie into later requests.

advisories.summary: Mechanize sends credential headers to another host after an HTTP redirect

fix_commits.message_title: fix: strip Proxy-Authorization and Cookie2 on cross-host redirect
fix: request_headers no longer follow a redirect across sites
fix: a withheld credential stays withheld for the whole operation
fix_commits.role: follow-up (withheld credential stays withheld for the whole operation)

instances.mechanism: Cross-host redirects stripped only Authorization and Cookie, and headers set at agent level were re-applied on every hop; the fix adds Proxy-Authorization and Cookie2 and stops re-applying withheld headers after a cross-origin hop.
instances.notes: Fix spans three commits; all three are linked by the advisory. Same repository as CVE-2022-31033.

fix_commits.message_title: url: ntlm/negotiate, prohibit connection reuse on follows

instances.mechanism: With Negotiate authentication and an ambient Kerberos user, a followed request could pick a connection set up for the first origin and pass the credentials on to the redirect target; the fix forbids NTLM and Negotiate connection matching on follows unless auth to that host is allowed.
instances.notes: No GHSA and no NVD entry yet (announced 2026-10-14); advisory date taken from curl.se. Credential leak through connection reuse rather than through a header copy.

advisories.summary: Reactor Netty HTTP is vulnerable to credential leaks during chained redirects

fix_commits.message_title: Ensure the HTTP/2 upgrade stream inherits the proper state from the original HTTP/1.1 connection when successful upgrade from HTTP/1.1 to HTTP/2 (#3838)
fix_commits.role: commit referenced by the advisory (does not match)

instances.mechanism: In some chained-redirect scenarios the client forwarded credentials to a later redirect target (advisory text; fix not located).
instances.notes: The only commit referenced by the advisory is about HTTP/2 upgrade stream state and does not touch redirect or credential handling. No public commit implementing the fix was found; excluded from counts.

families.name: HTTP client forwards credentials (Authorization, Cookie, Proxy-Authorization, tokens) when following a redirect to another host, scheme or port

advisories.summary: Symlink Arbitrary File Overwrite in tar

fix_commits.message_title: extract: normalize symbolic links outside root

instances.mechanism: Symbolic link entries could point outside the extraction root and later entries were written through them; the fix rewrites any linkpath that resolves outside the root so it stays inside.
instances.notes: Advisory links only an npm/npm release; the fix is the link-handling commit in v1.0.3...v2.0.0 (the other code commit there only emits finish). Repository was npm/node-tar (redirects to isaacs/node-tar).

advisories.summary: Directory traversal vulnerability in RubyZip

fix_commits.message_title: Fix #315 and resolve relative path vulnerability

instances.mechanism: Entry#extract wrote entries named with '../' components relative to the destination; the fix skips entries whose name contains a '..' path component.
instances.notes: Incomplete: absolute paths and symlinks still escaped, which became CVE-2018-1000544. No test file in the commit.

advisories.summary: Kubernetes arbitrary file overwrite

instances.mechanism: kubectl cp untarred the archive produced by the container and joined each header name to the local destination, so '../' names escaped it; the fix cleans every name as a rooted path before joining.
instances.notes: Advisory links only issue #61297; PR #61298 found from the issue timeline. The GHSA was imported in 2022, NVD date is the real disclosure date.

advisories.summary: Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction in unzipper

instances.mechanism: Extract joined each entry path to the destination without a containment check; the fix skips entries whose joined path does not start with the destination path.
instances.notes: Containment is a plain string-prefix test without a trailing separator, the weakness later exploited in tar-fs (CVE-2025-59343) and decompress (CVE-2026-53486).

advisories.summary: Arbitrary File Write in adm-zip

instances.mechanism: extractEntryTo and extractAllTo resolved entry names against the target directory without checking the result; the fix throws when the resolved path does not start with the target path.
instances.notes: Prefix check without trailing separator. No test file in the commit.

advisories.summary: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory in zt-zip

fix_commits.message_title: Fixed potential security vulnerability reported by Snyk Security Research Team

instances.mechanism: Unpacking created files at outputDir + entry name, so names with '..' landed outside; the fix rejects entries containing '..' whose canonical path does not start with the canonical output directory.

advisories.summary: Improper Input Validation in tar-fs

fix_commits.message_title: force hardlink targets to be in the tar

instances.mechanism: Hard link entries resolved their target with path.resolve(cwd, linkname), so absolute or '../' link names pointed outside the extraction directory; the fix joins a rooted, normalised linkname under cwd.
instances.notes: No test file in the commit. Reported together with the node-tar hardlink issue (same HackerOne report).

advisories.summary: Arbitrary File Overwrite in tar

fix_commits.message_title: unpack: only reuse file fs entries if nlink = 1
Bump fstream to fix hardlink overwriting vulnerability
fix_commits.role: fix for 2.x (bumps fstream, adds regression test)

instances.mechanism: A hard link to a file outside the destination followed by a regular file entry with the same name made the extractor write through the existing inode; the fix only reuses an existing file when its link count is 1.
instances.notes: The 2.x line got its fix a year later through fstream (CVE-2019-13173).

advisories.summary: Directory Traversal in SharpCompress

fix_commits.message_title: fix: prevent extracting archived files outside of target path

instances.mechanism: WriteToDirectory combined the entry key with the destination directory without checking the result; the fix computes full paths and throws when the target directory or file is not under the destination.
instances.notes: Prefix check (StartsWith) on full paths.

advisories.summary: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory in plexus-archiver

instances.mechanism: AbstractUnArchiver resolved entry names against the destination without a containment check; the fix throws when the canonical entry path does not start with the canonical destination.

advisories.summary: DotNetZip Zip-Slip Vulnerability

instances.mechanism: Entry paths containing '../' were used as-is on extraction; the fix sanitises them by dropping parent-directory segments that would climb above the top directory.
instances.notes: Tests live under 'src/Zip Tests/'.

advisories.summary: Arbitrary file overwrite in tar-rs

instances.mechanism: Hard link entries could point at files outside the destination and later regular-file entries were written through existing links; the fix validates hard-link sources inside the destination and removes an existing path before creating a regular file.
instances.notes: Repository moved from alexcrichton/tar-rs to composefs/tar-rs.

advisories.summary: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory in SharpZipLib

fix_commits.message_title: Restrict path traversal on FastZip extraction (#235)

instances.mechanism: FastZip extraction accepted names with '../' and wrote outside the target folder; the fix makes the name transform reject parent traversal unless the caller opts in.
instances.notes: Advisory links only issue #232; the commit closing it was taken from the issue timeline. Its base-directory prefix check is what CVE-2021-32842 later bypassed.

advisories.summary: Rubyzip gem contains a Directory Traversal vulnerability in zip file component

instances.mechanism: The 2017 '..' filter missed absolute paths and symlink entries, so archives still wrote outside the destination; the fix checks that the cleaned entry name is relative and stays under the root, and disables symlink extraction.
instances.notes: Incomplete-fix recurrence: the advisory says the CVE-2017-5946 fix was incomplete.

advisories.summary: Symlink Attack in kubectl cp

instances.mechanism: kubectl cp still created symlinks from the archive with arbitrary targets and accepted names outside the expected prefix; the fix rejects entries outside the prefix and symlinks whose target leaves the destination.
instances.notes: Second kubectl cp traversal fix.

advisories.summary: The kubectl cp command allows copying files between containers and the user machine. To copy...

instances.mechanism: The previous fix could still be bypassed through link handling in the untar code; the fix reworks link processing and checks each destination against the target directory after resolving links.
instances.notes: Third kubectl cp fix (incomplete fix of CVE-2019-1002101).

advisories.summary: Arbitrary File Overwrite in fstream

fix_commits.message_title: Clobber a Link if it's in the way of a File

instances.mechanism: When a file entry targeted a path that already existed as a hard link, the writer opened it and overwrote the linked file outside the extraction directory; the fix removes the existing entry first when its link count is above 1.
instances.notes: Same trick as node-tar CVE-2018-20834, in the library used by tar 2.x. Archived repository. No test file in this commit (node-tar added one).

advisories.summary: The kubectl cp command allows copying files between containers and the user machine. To copy...

instances.mechanism: The earlier kubectl cp fixes could be bypassed, letting entries land outside the destination; the fix checks every joined destination path (and the path with symlinks evaluated) against the destination before creating it.
instances.notes: Kubernetes issue #80984 calls it an incomplete fix for CVE-2019-1002101 and CVE-2019-11246; the PR title ('Refactors to kubectl CP command') does not say it is a security fix.

advisories.summary: Kubernetes kubectl cp Vulnerable to Symlink Attack

instances.mechanism: Symlink entries in the copied archive could still be used to escape the destination; the fix removes symlink support from kubectl cp entirely.
instances.notes: Fifth kubectl cp fix in 18 months.

advisories.summary: Path Traversal in Ansible

fix_commits.message_title: ansible-galaxy - Fix tar path traversal issue during install - CVE-2020-10691 (#68596)
ansible-galaxy - Fix tar path traversal issue during install - CVE-2020-10691 - 2.9 (#68601)
fix_commits.role: backport (stable-2.9), the commit linked by the advisory

instances.mechanism: ansible-galaxy collection install extracted tar members listed in FILES.json without checking where they land; the fix raises an error for members that would be written outside the collection directory.

advisories.summary: Path Traversal in decompress

instances.mechanism: An archive could create a symlink and then a file entry beneath it, writing outside the output directory; the fix checks the real path of each parent directory against the real output path and refuses to write into existing symlinks.
instances.notes: The containment test is realParentPath.indexOf(realOutputPath) !== 0 (prefix only). The maintained fork fixed that in 2026 (CVE-2026-53486); upstream remains unpatched for 2026 advisories.

advisories.summary: Path Traversal in MHolt Archiver

fix_commits.message_title: Prevent arbitrary file overwrite via path traversal (Zip Slip attack)

instances.mechanism: The tar, zip and rar unarchivers joined header names to the destination without validation; the fix adds a CheckPath that rejects names whose joined path does not have the absolute destination as prefix.
instances.notes: Authored 2019-05-11 but committed (merged) 2020-09-28. Prefix test without separator. A later advisory on the same project (CVE-2025-3445) has no fix: the commit it links only edits the README.

advisories.summary: Arbitrary File Creation/Overwrite due to insufficient absolute path sanitization

fix_commits.message_title: fix: strip absolute paths more comprehensively

instances.mechanism: Absolute paths were sanitised by removing a single root, so '////home/user/.bashrc' stayed absolute; the fix strips roots repeatedly until the path is relative.

advisories.summary: Arbitrary File Creation/Overwrite via insufficient symlink protection due to directory cache poisoning

fix_commits.message_title: Remove paths from dirCache when no longer dirs
Remove paths from dirCache when no longer dirs
Remove paths from dirCache when no longer dirs

instances.mechanism: The cache of directories already created still said 'directory' after an archive replaced that path with a symlink, so later entries were written through the symlink; the fix evicts a path and its children from the cache when a non-directory entry replaces it.
instances.notes: 85d3a942b4064e4ff171f91696fced7975167349, also linked by the advisory, is a duplicate of the same change on another branch.

advisories.summary: Arbitrary File Creation/Overwrite via insufficient symlink protection due to directory cache poisoning using symbolic links

fix_commits.message_title: fix: normalize paths on Windows systems

instances.mechanism: The directory-cache check treated backslash as a separator on POSIX and compared names case-sensitively, so a symlink named with backslashes or different case escaped the cache poisoning fix; the fix normalises separators only on Windows and prunes the cache case-insensitively.
instances.notes: Advisory has no commit link; commit identified with the v6.1.6...v6.1.7 compare. Incomplete-fix recurrence of CVE-2021-32803 one week later.

advisories.summary: Links in archive can create arbitrary directories

fix_commits.message_title: Don't create directories before we've verified they're inside the tar destination (#259)

instances.mechanism: Parent directories of an entry were created with create_dir_all before checking that they were inside the destination, so a symlink in the archive led directory creation outside it; the fix creates missing ancestors one by one after validating each parent.
instances.notes: Advisory links PR #259; the PR head commit (d5dd7f3180b6bf41c54129d31d334fea0e793de1) is not on main, the squash commit is.

advisories.summary: Arbitrary File Creation/Overwrite via insufficient symlink protection due to directory cache poisoning using symbolic links

fix_commits.message_title: fix: prune dirCache properly for unicode, windows
fix: reserve paths properly for unicode, windows
fix_commits.role: primary part 2 (6.x, path reservations for unicode)

instances.mechanism: Names that differ only by Unicode normalisation map to the same file on some filesystems but not in the extractor's cache and reservation keys, so the symlink checks could be bypassed; the fix normalises names (NFKD and case) for both.
instances.notes: Fix spans two commits on each release line; the advisory links all six.

advisories.summary: Arbitrary File Creation/Overwrite on Windows via insufficient relative path sanitization

fix_commits.message_title: fix: prevent path escape using drive-relative paths
fix: prevent path escape using drive-relative paths
fix: prevent path escape using drive-relative paths

instances.mechanism: On Windows a drive-relative path like 'c:../foo' was neither absolute nor seen as containing '..', so it escaped the target; the fix strips drive roots, rejects 'c:..' segments and checks the resolved path stays under cwd.

advisories.summary: Path Traversal in SharpZipLib
Path Traversal in SharpZipLib

fix_commits.message_title: test: add tests for tar path traversal

instances.mechanism: TarArchive checked containment with GetFullPath(destFile).StartsWith(destDir), which accepts sibling paths sharing the prefix such as /dir.sh for /dir; the fix compares the destination file's directory instead.
instances.notes: Only source change between v1.3.2 and v1.3.3. The CVE-2021-32840 advisory links only the test commit. CVE-2021-32842 (same prefix flaw in FastZip, introduced by the 2018 fix) has no visible fix commit in 1.3.3 and is left out.

advisories.summary: JSZip contains Path Traversal via loadAsync

fix_commits.message_title: Sanitize filenames with `loadAsync` to prevent zip slip attacks

instances.mechanism: loadAsync kept entry names containing '../', so callers that wrote files by entry name escaped their directory; the fix resolves names to a safe relative form and keeps the raw name in unsafeOriginalName.
instances.notes: Commit also rebuilds dist/ bundles.

advisories.summary: Directory traversal vulnerability in the (1) extract and (2) extractall functions in the tarfile...

fix_commits.message_title: gh-102950: Implement PEP 706 – Filter for tarfile.extractall (#102953)
gh-121999: Change default tarfile filter to 'data' (GH-122002)

instances.fixed_version: 3.12 (filters, with backports to 3.8-3.11 security releases); 'data' filter default in 3.14
instances.mechanism: tarfile extract/extractall honoured absolute names, '..' components and links pointing outside the destination; the fix adds extraction filters that reject or sanitise such members and later makes the safe filter the default.
instances.notes: The GHSA (imported 2022) links only 2007 mailing-list posts; neither commit message cites the CVE (PEP 706 does). Between 2023 and 3.14 the protection is opt-in, so treat as a two-step fix. Very large diff (604-line tarfile.py patch).

advisories.summary: Arbitrary File Creation in AbstractUnArchiver

fix_commits.message_title: Avoid override target symlink by standard file in AbstractUnArchiver

instances.mechanism: An archive could create a symlink and then a regular-file entry with the same name, and writing the file followed the link outside the destination; the fix refuses to overwrite an existing symlink with a regular file.
instances.notes: Same repository as CVE-2018-1002200.

advisories.summary: Ansible symlink attack vulnerability

fix_commits.message_title: Prevent roles from using symlinks to overwrite files outside of the installation directory (#81780)
[stable-2.15] Prevent roles from using symlinks to overwrite files outside of the installation directory (#81780) (#81785)
fix_commits.role: backport (stable-2.15), the commit linked by the advisory

instances.mechanism: Role installation sanitised member names but not symlink targets, so a role archive could write through a link pointing outside the roles directory; the fix applies the same sanitising to linkname.
instances.notes: Same repository as CVE-2020-10691 (collections then, roles now).

advisories.summary: unzip-stream allows Arbitrary File Write via artifact extraction

instances.mechanism: The path sanitiser only removed '../' sequences at the start of the entry path, so 'a/../../x' escaped; the fix neutralises every '..' component.
instances.notes: No CVE. No test file in the commit.

advisories.summary: tar-fs Vulnerable to Link Following and Path Traversal via Extracting a Crafted tar File

fix_commits.message_title: refactor and throw on bad symlink

instances.mechanism: Symlink entries were created with arbitrary targets, letting later entries be written through them; the fix throws when a symlink's resolved target is not inside cwd.
instances.notes: Containment written as dst.startsWith(cwd), which CVE-2025-59343 showed to be prefix-only.

advisories.summary: tar-fs can extract outside the specified dir with a specific tarball

instances.mechanism: Directory entries were created before the path validation that file entries went through, so a crafted tarball could still place content outside the target; the fix validates directories (and link targets) before creating them.
instances.notes: No test file in the commit.

advisories.summary: Allows arbitrary filesystem writes outside the extraction directory during extraction with filter...
Allows the extraction filter to be ignored, allowing symlink targets to point outside the...
Allows the extraction filter to be ignored, allowing symlink targets to point outside the...
Allows modifying some file metadata (e.g. last modified) with filter="data" or file permissions ...

fix_commits.message_title: gh-135034: Normalize link targets in tarfile, add `os.path.realpath(strict='allow_missing')` (#135037)
[3.13] gh-135034: Normalize link targets in tarfile, add `os.path.realpath(strict='allow_missing')` (GH-135037) (GH-135064)
[3.12] gh-135034: Normalize link targets in tarfile, add `os.path.realpath(strict='allow_missing')` (GH-135037) (GH-135066)

instances.mechanism: The data and tar extraction filters relied on os.path.realpath, which stops resolving on long or missing paths, and kept non-normalised link targets, so crafted symlink chains passed the filter and wrote or linked outside the destination; the fix resolves with realpath(strict=ALLOW_MISSING), normalises linknames and rejects unsafe link fallbacks.
instances.notes: One fix for four advisories; the commit message names all four CVEs. Bypass of the 2023 PEP 706 filters in the same repository.

advisories.summary: tar-fs has a symlink validation bypass if destination directory is predictable with a specific tarball

instances.mechanism: The containment test dst.startsWith(cwd) accepted sibling directories whose names start with the destination name; the fix requires equality or a cwd + path.sep prefix.
instances.notes: Third tar-fs fix in 2025; incomplete-fix recurrence of CVE-2024-12905. No test file in the commit.

advisories.summary: pip's fallback tar extraction doesn't check symbolic links point to extraction directory

instances.mechanism: On Pythons without PEP 706, pip's fallback tar extraction created symlinks without checking their targets; the fix refuses symlinks that do not point to a member inside the archive.

advisories.summary: node-tar is Vulnerable to Arbitrary File Overwrite and Symlink Poisoning via Insufficient Path Sanitization

instances.mechanism: Absolute-path stripping and '..' checks applied to entry paths but not to the linkpath of hard links and symlinks, so an absolute link target pointed outside the root; the fix sanitises linkpath the same way.
instances.notes: Start of a 2026 series of six node-tar link-handling advisories in eight weeks.

advisories.summary: Race Condition in node-tar Path Reservations via Unicode Ligature Collisions on macOS APFS

instances.mechanism: Path reservations normalised names without folding Unicode ligatures that APFS treats as equal, so a symlink and a file entry could race on the same location; the fix normalises ligatures out of reservation keys.
instances.notes: Race condition rather than a direct traversal; same idea as CVE-2021-37712.

advisories.summary: node-tar Vulnerable to Arbitrary File Creation/Overwrite via Hardlink Path Traversal

fix_commits.message_title: fix: properly sanitize hard links containing ..

instances.mechanism: The January linkpath sanitiser allowed '..' in link targets (needed for relative symlinks) for hard links too, so a hard link with '../' escaped; the fix rejects '..' for hard links.
instances.notes: Incomplete fix of CVE-2026-23745 eleven days earlier.

advisories.summary: Compressing Vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write via Symlink Extraction

fix_commits.message_title: fix: prevent arbitrary file write via symlink extraction (#133)

instances.mechanism: Tar extraction joined header names and symlink targets to the destination without checks; the fix rejects entries and symlink targets that resolve outside the destination, using a separator-aware prefix test.

advisories.summary: Arbitrary File Read/Write via Hardlink Target Escape Through Symlink Chain in node-tar Extraction

fix_commits.message_title: fix: do not write linkpaths through symlinks
fix(unpack): improve UnpackSync symlink error "into" path accuracy

instances.mechanism: A chain of symlinks created earlier in the archive let a hard link target resolve outside the root while each string check passed; the fix refuses to create link entries whose target goes through a symlink.

advisories.summary: tar has Hardlink Path Traversal via Drive-Relative Linkpath

fix_commits.message_title: parse root off paths before sanitizing .. parts

instances.mechanism: The '..' check on linkpaths ran before the drive root was stripped, so a hard link target like 'c:../x' passed; the fix strips the root first and then checks the parts.
instances.notes: CVE-2021-37713 (drive-relative paths) came back for linkpaths.

advisories.summary: node-tar Symlink Path Traversal via Drive-Relative Linkpath

fix_commits.message_title: prevent escaping symlinks with drive-relative paths

instances.mechanism: The symlink escape check resolved the original drive-relative linkpath instead of the stripped parts, so a symlink could still escape; the fix resolves the sanitised parts.
instances.notes: Fix for the symlink case six days after CVE-2026-29786 fixed the hard-link case.

advisories.summary: Complete Bypass of CVE-2026-24884 Patch via Git-Delivered Symlink Poisoning in compressing

fix_commits.message_title: fix: prevent symlink path traversal via pre-existing symlinks during tar extraction

instances.mechanism: The containment check from the January fix was purely string-based, so a symlink already present under the destination redirected writes outside it; the fix walks each path segment with lstat/realpath and fails closed.
instances.notes: The advisory title calls it a complete bypass of the CVE-2026-24884 patch.

advisories.summary: Decompress: Archive extraction can create files and links outside of the target directory

fix_commits.message_title: Validate link targets to prevent escaping the output directory

fix_commits.role: part of fix (path.relative instead of prefix test)

fix_commits.message_title: Strip setuid/setgid/sticky bits from extracted files

instances.mechanism: Hard links and symlinks were created without checking their targets, and containment was a string-prefix test inherited from the 2020 upstream fix; the fix validates link targets against the output directory and uses path.relative for containment.
instances.notes: Maintained fork of kevva/decompress; the advisory says upstream has the same flaws and no fix. Cross-repository recurrence of CVE-2020-12265's weak check. The advisory links short SHAs, resolved through the API.

advisories.summary: @actions/artifact has an Arbitrary File Write via artifact extraction

fix_commits.role: commit linked by the advisory (dependency bump)

instances.mechanism: Artifact download extraction let zip entries with traversal names write outside the target directory.
instances.notes: Excluded from counts. The linked commit only bumps unzip-stream (which received its own fix) and reverts to unzip.Extract. The earlier in-repo check rejects the promise on a bad path but does not stop the write. The advisory text (fixed in 2.1.7) and its version range (fixed in 2.1.2) disagree.

families.name: Archive extraction writes outside the destination directory (zip slip / tar slip: '..', absolute or drive paths, symlink and hardlink tricks, prefix-only containment checks)

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution Protection Bypass in qs

fix_commits.message_title: [Fix] ensure that `allowPrototypes: false` does not ever shadow Object.prototype properties.

instances.mechanism: Bracket keys such as ']=' slipped past the allowPrototypes:false guard, so a query string could overwrite Object.prototype method names on the parsed object; the fix tightens the parent-key regex and bracket stripping so the guard always applies.
instances.notes: Shadows prototype properties on the result object rather than polluting the global prototype.

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in lodash

fix_commits.message_title: Avoid merging properties on to __proto__ objects.

instances.mechanism: merge, mergeWith and defaultsDeep read object['__proto__'] as the destination for a nested merge, so a source with a __proto__ key wrote onto Object.prototype; the fix reads keys through a safeGet that returns undefined for __proto__.
instances.notes: First of five lodash advisories in this family.

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in hoek

instances.mechanism: Hoek.merge copied every own key of the source, including a __proto__ key from JSON.parse, into the target; the fix skips __proto__.

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in merge-deep

instances.mechanism: The recursive merge copied a __proto__ key from the source onto the target; the fix skips that key.
instances.notes: Only __proto__ is blocked; constructor/prototype became CVE-2021-26707. No test file in the commit.

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in deep-extend

instances.mechanism: deepExtend read target['__proto__'] and recursed into it when a source carried that key; the fix reads properties through a helper that returns undefined for __proto__.
instances.notes: Commit also deletes yarn.lock.

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in lodash

fix_commits.message_title: Ensure Object.prototype is not augmented by _.merge.

instances.mechanism: With __proto__ blocked, merge could still reach Object.prototype through a constructor.prototype path; safeGet now also refuses a 'prototype' key whose value is Object.prototype.
instances.notes: Incomplete-fix recurrence of CVE-2018-3721 in the same helper.

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in merge

instances.mechanism: The merge loop copied a __proto__ key from the source object into the target; the fix skips that key.
instances.notes: Advisory has no commit link; found as the only fix commit before tag v1.2.1. Repository renamed from yeikos/js.merge. The recursive merge path was fixed only in 2021 (CVE-2020-28499).

advisories.summary: XSS in jQuery as used in Drupal, Backdrop CMS, and other products

fix_commits.message_title: Core: Prevent Object.prototype pollution for $.extend( true, ... )

instances.mechanism: $.extend(true, ...) deep-copied a '__proto__' property from an untrusted object into the target's prototype chain; the fix skips the '__proto__' name.

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in mixin-deep

fix_commits.message_title: ensure keys are valid when mixing in values

instances.mechanism: The code already skipped __proto__ but still mixed in 'constructor' and 'prototype' keys, which reach Object.prototype; the fix rejects all three keys.
instances.notes: No test file in these commits.

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in set-value

fix_commits.message_title: ensure only valid keys are used

instances.mechanism: set() split a dotted path and assigned along it, so '__proto__.x' or 'constructor.prototype.x' wrote onto Object.prototype; the fix filters those keys out of the path.
instances.notes: No test file in these commits.

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in lodash

instances.mechanism: defaultsDeep could still be steered onto Object.prototype with a {constructor: {prototype: ...}} payload; safeGet now also returns undefined for a 'constructor' key holding a function.
instances.notes: Third fix of the same safeGet helper. Advisory links only the PR.

advisories.summary: dot-prop Prototype Pollution vulnerability

fix_commits.message_title: Prevent setting/getting some problematic path components
feat: patch 4.2.0 with fixes for CVE-2020-8116

instances.mechanism: set/get/delete walked any dotted path, including __proto__, prototype and constructor segments; the fix treats a path containing those segments as empty.
instances.notes: Main fix landed in Oct 2019, the advisory in July 2020.

advisories.summary: hoek subject to prototype pollution via the clone function.

fix_commits.message_title: Prevent prototype poisoning in clone(). Closes #352

instances.mechanism: clone() copied a __proto__ own key onto the new object, changing its prototype; the fix skips __proto__ while cloning.
instances.notes: Fixed in Feb 2020 but the CVE/GHSA only appeared in Sept 2022 (straddles the cutoff). Same repository and same missing check as CVE-2018-3728, in a different function.

advisories.summary: Prototype pollution in dojo

instances.mechanism: The deep-copy helper in request/util copied a __proto__ property from the source; the fix skips that name.
instances.notes: A later dojo advisory (CVE-2021-23450, setObject) has no patched version and is left out.

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in minimist

fix_commits.message_title: even more aggressive checks for protocol pollution
fix_commits.role: follow-up the same day (complete check, released in 1.2.3)

instances.mechanism: setKey assigned nested option names such as --__proto__.x along the path and could land on Object.prototype; the fix stops on __proto__ keys and replaces built-in prototypes met on the path with fresh objects.
instances.notes: Two commits on the main line; for a before/after pair use the parent of the first and the second commit. 'constructor' was still allowed, which became CVE-2021-44906. The advisory's source repository substack/minimist no longer exists on GitHub; minimistjs/minimist is the maintained continuation and carries these commits.
instances.repo_history: continuation of substack/minimist, which no longer exists on GitHub

advisories.summary: yargs-parser Vulnerable to Prototype Pollution

fix_commits.message_title: fix: __proto__ will now be replaced with ___proto___ in parse (#258)

instances.mechanism: Dot-notation options were assigned key by key, so --__proto__.x set a property on Object.prototype; the fix renames __proto__ path segments to ___proto___.
instances.notes: The advisory also links 1c417bd0b42b09c475ee881e36d292af4fa2cc36, which only adds release automation for the 5.x backport branch.

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in lodash

instances.mechanism: zipObjectDeep built nested objects along user paths without checking path segments; the fix stops when a segment is __proto__, constructor or prototype.

advisories.summary: flat vulnerable to Prototype Pollution

instances.mechanism: unflatten turned keys like '__proto__.polluted' into nested assignments that reached Object.prototype; the fix returns early when a key segment is __proto__.
instances.notes: Committed Aug 2020, advisory Dec 2022 (straddles the cutoff). No test file in the commit.

advisories.summary: Prototype pollution in json-pointer

instances.mechanism: set() walked JSON-pointer tokens and created intermediate objects even for __proto__, constructor or prototype tokens; the fix skips those tokens.
instances.notes: Skipping (continue) rather than rejecting; bypassed with non-string tokens (CVE-2021-23820 / CVE-2022-4742). Advisory links only the PR.

advisories.summary: Prototype pollution in object-path

instances.mechanism: In inherited-props mode set() followed __proto__ or a constructor function while walking the path; the fix throws when the current segment is __proto__ or a function-valued constructor.
instances.notes: The commit also reformats test.js (large diff).

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in y18n

instances.mechanism: The locale cache was a plain object, so a locale named __proto__ made later writes land on Object.prototype; the fix creates the cache with Object.create(null).
instances.notes: Main fix Oct 2020 (NVD Nov 2020), GHSA March 2021, 3.x backport Jan 2021.

advisories.summary: ini before 1.3.6 vulnerable to Prototype Pollution via ini.parse

fix_commits.message_title: do not allow invalid hazardous string as section name

instances.mechanism: ini.parse used section and key names from the file as object keys, so a [__proto__] section or __proto__ key polluted the prototype; the fix ignores those names.

advisories.summary: Prototype pollution in Merge-deep

fix_commits.message_title: add isValidKey function to ensure only valid keys are merged

instances.mechanism: The 2018 fix only skipped __proto__, so constructor.prototype keys still reached Object.prototype; the fix rejects __proto__, constructor and prototype.
instances.notes: Incomplete-fix recurrence of CVE-2018-3722 in the same line of code. Committed 2021-01-04, just after the cutoff. No test file in the commit.

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in immer

fix_commits.message_title: fix: Fixed security issue #738: prototype pollution possible when applying patches CVE-2020-28477

instances.mechanism: applyPatches walked patch paths through any key, so a path through __proto__ or constructor.prototype modified built-in prototypes; the fix refuses those segments.
instances.notes: Committed 2021-01-20.

advisories.summary: dset vulnerable to prototype pollution

instances.mechanism: dset assigned along the key path without checking segments, so __proto__ or constructor.prototype paths polluted Object.prototype; the fix skips those keys.
instances.notes: The commit linked by the GHSA (2b9ec49e231107b1a83b04a1bc1a66a8d14cea1c, 2018) only changes array creation for float keys and does not address pollution; the NVD text says versions through 2.0.1 are affected, and the real fix is the 2021-01-27 commit recorded here. Skips (continue) rather than stops, later reworked.

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in merge

instances.mechanism: The recursive merge helper copied __proto__, constructor and prototype keys, unlike the guarded non-recursive path fixed in 2018; the fix skips them there too.
instances.notes: Same repository as CVE-2018-16469 (different code path). Commit also rebuilds dist/.

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in mout

instances.mechanism: object/set assigned along a dotted path without filtering, so __proto__ or constructor.prototype paths polluted Object.prototype; the fix refuses props containing those words.
instances.notes: CVE published Dec 2020 but the fix was merged July 2021 and the GHSA came in 2022. The check uses prop.includes(), which for an array prop tests elements, hence CVE-2022-21213. No test file in the commit.

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in object-path

fix_commits.message_title: Fix prototype pollution when path components are not strings

instances.mechanism: The 0.11.5 check compared path segments to '__proto__' with ===, so a non-string segment like ['__proto__'] passed and was coerced to the key later; the fix converts segments to strings before checking.
instances.notes: Type-confusion bypass of CVE-2020-15256.

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in set-value

instances.mechanism: Unsafe-key checks compared path components to strings, so an array component such as ['__proto__'] bypassed them; the fix stringifies non-string, non-number keys before validation.
instances.notes: Type-confusion bypass of the CVE-2019-10747 fix. The advisory also links 7cf8073bb06bf0c15e08475f9f952823b4576452, which is only the 4.0.1 version bump.

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in immer

fix_commits.message_title: fix(security): Follow up on CVE-2020-28477 where `path: [["__proto__"], "x"]` could still pollute the prototype

instances.mechanism: The CVE-2020-28477 guard compared path segments with ===, so a segment given as ['__proto__'] passed; the fix coerces each segment to a string first.
instances.notes: Type-confusion bypass seven months after the first fix.

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in object-path

instances.mechanism: del, empty, push and insert in inherited-props mode still followed magic properties that set() now refused; the fix applies the same magic-property check to them.
instances.notes: Third object-path advisory in a year. The commit also reformats index.js (semicolons), so the diff is noisy.

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in node-jsonpointer

instances.mechanism: set() only rejected __proto__ or constructor/prototype as the first pointer segments and accepted array segments; the fix checks every segment and rejects non-string, non-number segments.
instances.notes: The removed lines show an older first-segment-only guard.

advisories.summary: qs vulnerable to Prototype Pollution

instances.mechanism: qs.parse created a property named __proto__ from 'a[__proto__]=...' input, changing the parsed object's prototype and letting a request hang express; the fix ignores __proto__ keys while building the object.
instances.notes: Fixed Dec 2021, advisory Nov 2022. The advisory links nine commits, one per release line, all with the same change.

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in json-pointer
json-pointer vulnerable to Prototype Pollution

instances.mechanism: The 0.6.1 token check compared tokens to strings, so a pointer given as an array with a nested ['__proto__'] token bypassed it; the fix stringifies non-string, non-number tokens first.
instances.notes: Two CVEs, one fix. The CVE-2021-23820 advisory links 931b0f9c7178ca09778087b4b0ac7e4f505620c2, which is only the 0.6.2 release commit (package-lock and version).

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in minimist

instances.mechanism: setKey blocked __proto__ but not a function-valued 'constructor', so --constructor.prototype.x still reached Object.prototype; the fix adds an isConstructorOrProto check on every path segment.
instances.notes: Incomplete-fix recurrence of CVE-2020-7598. The 0.2.4 backport wrote the helper with wrong operator grouping (key === 'constructor' && (... || key === '__proto__')), corrected in Feb 2023.
instances.repo_history: continuation of substack/minimist, which no longer exists on GitHub

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in dset

instances.mechanism: dset/merge checked unsafe keys only on the top-level path, while its internal merge() copied nested __proto__ keys; the fix makes merge() stop on __proto__, constructor and prototype.
instances.notes: No test file in this commit (tests added in 845879b the same day).

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in protobufjs

fix_commits.message_title: fix: do not let setProperty change the prototype (#1731)
fix: do not let setProperty change the prototype (#1731)
fix_commits.role: same change on the 6.x branch, linked by the advisory

instances.mechanism: util.setProperty, used when parsing options, walked dotted paths including __proto__; the fix returns early on a __proto__ segment.
instances.notes: No test file in the commit.

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in mout

instances.mechanism: The 2021 guard called prop.includes(), which on an array checks elements instead of the joined path, so an array prop bypassed it; the fix stringifies prop before checking and before use.
instances.notes: Type-confusion bypass of the CVE-2020-7792 fix. Commit also regenerates package-lock.json.

advisories.summary: Prototype Pollution in JSON5 via Parse Method

fix_commits.message_title: fix: add __proto__ to objects and arrays
fix: add __proto__ to objects and arrays

instances.mechanism: parse() stored keys with plain assignment, so a '__proto__' key set the prototype of the returned object instead of creating a property; the fix defines properties with Object.defineProperty.
instances.notes: Pollutes the parsed object's prototype rather than Object.prototype.

advisories.summary: protobufjs Prototype Pollution vulnerability

fix_commits.message_title: fix: do not let setProperty change the prototype (#1899)

instances.mechanism: The 2022 fix blocked only __proto__, so a constructor.prototype path in setProperty still polluted; the fix also stops on 'prototype'.
instances.notes: Incomplete-fix recurrence of CVE-2022-25878.

advisories.summary: dset Prototype Pollution vulnerability

fix_commits.message_title: fix: prevent __proto__ assignment via implicit string

instances.mechanism: Key checks compared path entries with ===, so an entry given as ['__proto__'] passed and was coerced on assignment; the fix converts each key to a string before checking.
instances.notes: Third dset advisory; same type-confusion bypass as set-value, object-path and immer in 2021.

advisories.summary: Lodash has Prototype Pollution Vulnerability in `_.unset` and `_.omit` functions

fix_commits.message_title: Prevent prototype pollution on baseUnset function

instances.mechanism: _.unset and _.omit walked any path and deleted the last key, so a path through __proto__ or constructor.prototype removed properties of built-in prototypes; the fix rejects those segments while walking.
instances.notes: Fifth lodash advisory of the family; deletion instead of assignment. The commit also rebuilds dist/.

families.name: Prototype pollution: deep merge, path setters, parsers or patch appliers write through __proto__ / constructor.prototype keys (including bypasses through non-string keys)

advisories.summary: HTTP Request Smuggling in Netty

fix_commits.message_title: Correctly handle whitespaces in HTTP header names as defined by RFC7230#section-3.2.4 (#9585)

instances.mechanism: The request decoder ended a header name at the first whitespace, so 'Transfer-Encoding : chunked' was accepted and treated as Transfer-Encoding while other servers ignore it; the fix stops treating whitespace as the end of a request header name so header validation rejects it.
instances.notes: Advisory links only an issue and the tag compare; commit found in netty-4.1.41.Final...netty-4.1.42.Final. Tests not in this commit.

advisories.summary: HTTP Request Smuggling in Netty

fix_commits.message_title: Detect missing colon when parsing http headers with no value (#9871)

instances.mechanism: A header line without any colon was accepted as a header with an empty value; the fix rejects lines with no colon.
instances.notes: Advisory links PR #9871; this is its commit on 4.1.

advisories.summary: HTTP Request Smuggling in Netty
HTTP Request Smuggling in Netty

fix_commits.message_title: Verify we do not receive multiple content-length headers or a content-length and transfer-encoding: chunked header when using HTTP/1.1 (#9865)

instances.mechanism: Requests carrying several Content-Length headers, or Content-Length together with chunked Transfer-Encoding, were accepted and framed by one of them; the fix rejects multiple Content-Length values and rejects Content-Length combined with chunked on HTTP/1.1.
instances.notes: Both advisories link PR #9865. NVD calls CVE-2020-7238 an incomplete fix for CVE-2019-16869 (' Transfer-Encoding' with leading whitespace plus a later Content-Length).

advisories.summary: HTTP Request Smuggling: LF vs CRLF handling in Waitress

fix_commits.message_title: Remove support for non CRLF line endings

instances.mechanism: The parser accepted a bare LF as a line terminator, so a request a front proxy saw as one header block could end earlier for waitress; the fix only accepts CRLF.

advisories.summary: HTTP Request Smuggling: Content-Length Sent Twice in Waitress

instances.mechanism: Two Content-Length headers were joined into '10, 10', int() failed and the length silently became 0; the fix rejects an unparsable Content-Length with 400.
instances.notes: No test file in this commit (tests added elsewhere in the same security merge).

advisories.summary: HTTP Request Smuggling: Invalid Transfer-Encoding in Waitress

instances.mechanism: Only an exact 'chunked' value enabled chunked parsing, so 'gzip, chunked' fell back to Content-Length framing; the fix parses the encoding list, requires chunked to be last and answers 501 for unsupported codings.
instances.notes: The advisory links the merge commit; the fix itself is one commit inside it.

advisories.summary: HTTP Request Smuggling in Waitress: Invalid whitespace characters in headers (Follow-up)

fix_commits.message_title: Remove accidental stripping of non-printable characters

instances.mechanism: Header values and Transfer-Encoding items were cleaned with a bare strip(), which also removes characters that are not HTTP whitespace, so a value a proxy considered invalid became 'chunked' for waitress; the fix only strips space and tab.
instances.notes: Follow-up to the 1.4.0 and 1.4.1 fixes within two weeks.

advisories.summary: HTTP Smuggling via Transfer-Encoding Header in Puma

fix_commits.role: same change on the 4.3 line, linked by the advisory

instances.mechanism: Transfer-Encoding was compared to 'chunked' as a whole, so a list value like 'gzip, chunked' was not treated as chunked and Content-Length was used instead; the fix splits the list and recognises chunked inside it.
instances.notes: No test file in the commit.

advisories.summary: HTTP Request Smuggling in hyper

fix_commits.message_title: fix(http1): fix server misinterpretting multiple Transfer-Encoding headers

instances.mechanism: With several Transfer-Encoding headers, a 'chunked' seen in an earlier header kept the message chunked even if the final coding was something else; the fix resets the chunked flag when a later Transfer-Encoding does not end in chunked.
instances.notes: Tests are inline in src/proto/h1/role.rs.

advisories.summary: Lenient Parsing of Content-Length Header When Prefixed with Plus Sign

fix_commits.message_title: fix(http1): reject content-lengths that have a plus sign prefix

instances.mechanism: Content-Length was parsed with the standard integer parser, which accepts a leading '+'; the fix parses digits only.
instances.notes: Same lenient-integer root cause as waitress CVE-2022-24761 and aiohttp CVE-2023-47627.

advisories.summary: Puma with proxy which forwards LF characters as line endings could allow HTTP request smuggling

fix_commits.role: primary (merge from the advisory fork, on main)

instances.mechanism: The Ragel grammar allowed any byte, including a bare LF, inside header values, so behind a proxy that treats LF as a line end the two disagreed on headers; the fix limits field values to printable characters and tab.

advisories.summary: HTTP request smuggling in netty

instances.mechanism: Control characters such as 0x1c-0x1f around a header name were stripped as whitespace, turning 'Transfer-Encoding\x1f' into a real Transfer-Encoding header; the fix stops stripping them and rejects them in header names.
instances.notes: Third netty fix in this family, same splitHeader routine as CVE-2019-16869.

advisories.summary: HTTP Request Smuggling in waitress

instances.mechanism: Content-Length and chunk sizes went through int(), which accepts '+10', '0x01' style or padded values, and chunk extensions were not validated; the fix requires plain digits for Content-Length, hex digits for chunk sizes and valid extension syntax.
instances.notes: Same repository as the 2019 waitress fixes; the 2019 fix rejected values int() refused but not values int() accepts too leniently.

advisories.summary: Puma HTTP Request/Response Smuggling vulnerability

fix_commits.role: same change on another release line
same change on another release line

instances.mechanism: An empty Content-Length was accepted and the chunked decoder mishandled a trailer section after the zero-length chunk; the fix rejects empty Content-Length and skips trailers correctly.

advisories.summary: AIOHTTP has problems in HTTP parser (the python one, not llhttp)

fix_commits.message_title: [PR #7661/85713a48 backport][3.8] Update Python parser for RFCs 9110/9112 (#7662)

instances.mechanism: The pure-Python parser accepted signed or otherwise non-digit Content-Length values, whitespace around header names and duplicated framing headers; the fix requires digit-only lengths, rejects padded names and duplicate singleton headers such as Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding.
instances.notes: Only the Python fallback parser was affected (not llhttp).

advisories.summary: Request smuggling leading to endpoint restriction bypass in Gunicorn

instances.mechanism: Transfer-Encoding values other than a single chunked were tolerated, including stacked chunked, identity and empty values, and chunked with Content-Length or on HTTP/1.0; the fix rejects these combinations and closes the connection.
instances.notes: Commit from Dec 2023, released and advised in April 2024.

families.name: HTTP/1.1 server parses message framing leniently (Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding, line endings, header-name syntax), letting a front proxy and the server disagree on request boundaries (request smuggling)

method.advisories: GitHub global advisory API (gh api /advisories?cve_id=... or /advisories/GHSA-...); NVD API 2.0 for CVE publication dates; curl.se advisories (curl/curl-www repository) for curl.
method.advisory_published: Earliest of: GHSA published_at, NVD published, vendor advisory date. GHSA dates for pre-2019 CVEs are often 2022 re-imports, hence the NVD date.
method.commit_date: committer date of the primary commit (when it landed); author dates are kept per commit.
method.commits: Every SHA was fetched with gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/commits/SHA; full 40-character SHAs come from the API response. Short SHAs in advisories were resolved the same way.
method.on_default_branch: true if the commit is an ancestor of the repository's current default branch (GitHub compare API); backports on release branches are false.
method.split: memory: first fix commit and advisory both before the cutoff; eval: first fix commit on or after the cutoff; straddle: fix before the cutoff but advisory after it (diff was public, advisory text was not).
method.test_files: Heuristic on paths (test/, tests/, spec/, __tests__/, fixtures/, testdata/, tap-snapshots/, '* Tests/' folders, test_*.py, *_test.go, *.test.js, *Test(s).cs|java, *_spec.rb, root test.js, urllib3 dummyserver/, Go testcert/).
method.verification: status=verified means the primary commit (and listed parts) was fetched and its diff visibly implements what the advisory describes. 'unverified' instances are kept for information and excluded from counts.
